findings.explanation: The code may enter an infinite loop if the bundle header does not contain two consecutive newline characters (10) within the first 65536 bytes. The check for headerEnd >= 0 is only performed after processing each chunk, but if the header is malformed and never finds the double newline, the loop will continue indefinitely. This could lead to a denial of service attack by sending a malicious bundle that never completes the header parsing.
findings.title: Potential infinite loop in bundle header parsing

findings.explanation: The code assumes that the headerEnd is valid and that the header is properly formatted, but there is no explicit check to ensure that headerEnd is within the bounds of the pending array. If headerEnd is not properly calculated, this could lead to out-of-bounds access when slicing the pending array. This could result in undefined behavior or security vulnerabilities.
